result.summary: In 2023 Altman mostly avoided giving dates for AGI. He called it a blurry, gradual transition and said he hoped for 'short timelines, slow takeoff'. The dated statements I found are a staged-release line at StrictlyVC (better this year and next year), a December TIME event quote about 2024 and the end of the decade, and TIME's paraphrase that he thinks AGI could come within four or five years. The recorded May 2023 'Governance of superintelligence' claim was not re-checked.

reply_text:
I found two 2023 statements with a date or time span attached and one TIME paraphrase. None of them repeats the claim you've already recorded. I didn't reach that one: I had no page openings left for "Governance of superintelligence" (2023-05-22), so it isn't re-reported.

- **StrictlyVC with Connie Loizos, January 2023.** This one carries the best weight. Altman described making ChatGPT "a little better this year … a little better next year". It's mainly a plan for staged releases, so you may decide it's borderline. The page is a LessWrong poster's lightly edited version of an automated transcript, so check it against the YouTube video.
- **A Year in TIME, 12 December 2023.** He said things would improve more in 2024 and that by the end of the decade "the world is going to be in an unbelievably better place". This is about what AI's progress will bring rather than a specific capability, and it comes only from TIME's report of the event.
- **TIME's CEO of the Year profile (6 December 2023).** It says Altman thinks AGI "could be reached sometime in the next four or five years". Those are the reporters' words, not a quote from him. I've listed it as coverage only; you may decide it doesn't meet the "his own words" rule.

Gaps in what I read:
- **Senate hearing (16 May) and Hard Fork (recorded mid-November):** the pages opened, but each transcript cut off early (the Hard Fork one at about 16 minutes). Nothing dated appeared in what I saw, but most of each transcript went unread.
- **Lex Fridman #367:** the transcript cut off before the AGI chapter.
- **Unchecked:** "Planning for AGI and beyond" (24 February) and TIME's June 2023 interview (time.com/6288584).
